screen.chromastudio.title: Chroma Studio
window.chromastudio.pin: Pin: keep this tab on screen while you play. The open key brings the window back.
window.chromastudio.pin.no_world: A window can only be pinned in a world.
window.chromastudio.fullscreen.forced: The game window is too small for anything but fullscreen.
command.chromastudio.bad_hex: "%s" isn't a colour. Use six hex digits, like #ff8800.
command.chromastudio.debug.not_ready: The block index is still being built.
command.chromastudio.unknown_block: There's no block called "%s". Give a block's id, like oak_planks, or a colour, like #ff8800.
command.chromastudio.export.usage: Give a palette's share string, then a layout, a format and "place" if you like: /chroma export chroma1:stone,andesite wall nbt
command.chromastudio.export.unclosed: The share string starts with a double quote and has none to close it.
command.chromastudio.export.unknown_opti: "%s" isn't a layout, a format or "place". The layouts are strip, wall, patch_grid, noise_clusters, height_gradient and dither, and the formats litematic and nbt.
command.chromastudio.export.bad_share: That share string can't be read. %s.
command.chromastudio.export.empty: Nothing was exported, as the palette has no blocks this game knows.
command.chromastudio.export.skipped: Left out: %s. A block is left out when this game doesn't have it or its state, or when the layout is full.
command.chromastudio.place.usage: Give the name of a file in the export folder: /chroma place chroma-stone-strip
command.chromastudio.place.done: Placed "%s" in Litematica at %s, %s, %s. It's selected, so Litematica's tools can move it.
export.chromastudio.litematica.missing: Litematica isn't installed, so there's nothing to place the schematic with. The file is still there.
export.chromastudio.litematica.no_world: A schematic can only be placed in a world.
export.chromastudio.litematica.unreadabl: Litematica couldn't read %s. The file is still there.
export.chromastudio.litematica.failed: Litematica couldn't place the schematic (%s). The file is still there.
settings.chromastudio.title: Chroma Studio settings
settings.chromastudio.reset.tip: Puts this group's settings back to their defaults.
settings.chromastudio.undo.tip: Puts this group's settings back to what they were when you opened this screen.
settings.chromastudio.undo.none: Nothing in this group has changed.
settings.chromastudio.reset_all.tip: Puts every setting back to its default. Key binds stay as they are.
settings.chromastudio.reset_all.confirm: Reset every setting to its default?
settings.chromastudio.undo_all.tip: Puts every setting back to what it was when you opened this screen.
settings.chromastudio.keys.tip: Change the mod's keys in the game's key binds screen.
settings.chromastudio.rememberWindow.tip: Reopens the window where you left it, at the same size and in the same mode. Off, it opens centred at its smallest size.
settings.chromastudio.startTab.tip: The tab the window shows the first time you open it. After that it reopens on the tab you last used.
settings.chromastudio.pinOpacity.tip: How solid a pinned window looks, from 0.2 to 1.
settings.chromastudio.theme.tip: The colours of the window and of this screen. Custom builds them from a colour of your own.
settings.chromastudio.customColour.tip: The colour the Custom window colour is built from. Text turns dark on a light colour and light on a dark one.
settings.chromastudio.customColour.off: Set Window colour to Custom to use a colour of your own.
settings.chromastudio.defaultFace.tip: The face of a block that matching looks at when the window opens. Side is the best of the four sides; Any is the best of all six.
settings.chromastudio.shading.tip: Compares faces as the game lights them: sides darker than the top, the bottom darkest.
settings.chromastudio.metric.tip: How the difference between two colours is measured. OKLab matches what the eye sees and is the best choice for most uses.
settings.chromastudio.resultCount.tip: How many blocks a match lists, from 3 to 60.
settings.chromastudio.viewingDistance.ti: How far away you'll look at the build. Further away, a texture's detail blurs into fewer colours. 192 means far.
settings.chromastudio.filterFullCube.tip: Starts matching with only full cubes listed.
settings.chromastudio.filterSolid.tip: Starts matching with only blocks you can't walk through listed.
settings.chromastudio.filterOpaque.tip: Starts matching with only blocks you can't see through listed.
settings.chromastudio.filterSurvival.tip: Starts matching without the blocks you can only get in creative mode, such as bedrock.
settings.chromastudio.showDeltaE.tip: Shows each result's colour difference as a number.
settings.chromastudio.technicalBlocks.ti: Also indexes blocks with no item in the creative inventory.
settings.chromastudio.statesSeparately.t: Lists one row for each state of a block rather than one row per block.
settings.chromastudio.statesCap.tip: The most states kept for one block, from 1 to 8.
Uses the average of an animated texture's frames. Off, only its first frame counts.
settings.chromastudio.cacheFolder.tip: Where the block index is kept between sessions. Leave empty for config/chromastudio/cache.
settings.chromastudio.rebuildOnReload.ti: Rebuilds the block index whenever resource packs reload.
settings.chromastudio.refresh.tip: Builds the block index again, reading every texture afresh. Use it after changing a resource pack's files while it is loaded, which the cache can't notice.
settings.chromastudio.biomeMode.tip: Where grass, leaves and water get their tint: where you stand, the biome chosen below, or every biome as a range.
settings.chromastudio.biome.tip: The biome used when Biome is set to Chosen, as an id like minecraft:plains.
settings.chromastudio.gradientSteps.tip: How many blocks a new gradient has, from 2 to 32.
settings.chromastudio.easing.tip: How a new gradient's colours are spaced between its stops.
settings.chromastudio.hueArc.tip: Which way round the colour wheel a new gradient goes between two stops.
settings.chromastudio.spreadMatching.tip: Prefers blocks whose textures are as busy as their neighbours in the gradient.
settings.chromastudio.generateCount.tip: How many colours Generate makes, from 2 to 32.
settings.chromastudio.captureCount.tip: How many of the commonest blocks Capture keeps, from 1 to 64.
settings.chromastudio.hotbarOverflowMode: Shulker boxes in a hotbar fill

Where Hotbar puts a palette's blocks past the ninth. Never: in free inventory slots, and any with no slot are dropped at your feet. When full: a shulker box only for those with no slot. Always: all of them go in shulker boxes.
settings.chromastudio.dioramaPerspective: How the 3D diorama is drawn. Orthographic keeps far blocks as big as near ones. Perspective makes them smaller, as the eye sees them.
settings.chromastudio.exportFolder.tip: Where exports are saved. Leave empty for Litematica's schematics folder, or the game's schematics folder without Litematica.
settings.chromastudio.defaultLayout.tip: How an export arranges the palette's blocks.
settings.chromastudio.patchSize.tip: The side of each block's square in the patch grid layout, from 1 to 16.
settings.chromastudio.exportGap.tip: Leaves one block of air between entries in an export.
settings.chromastudio.tooltipMode.tip: When an item's tooltip shows its colour: while you hold Shift, always or never.
settings.chromastudio.tooltipSwatch.tip: Shows the block's colour as a swatch.
settings.chromastudio.tooltipHex.tip: Shows the block's colour as a hex code.
settings.chromastudio.tooltipKind.tip: Shows what kind of block it is, such as slab or stairs.
settings.chromastudio.tooltipBadge.tip: Shows whether the texture is flat, grainy or busy.
settings.chromastudio.tooltipDeltaE.tip: Shows how far the block's colour is from the colour you're matching.
settings.chromastudio.readoutSeconds.tip: How long the eyedropper's readout stays on screen, from 1 to 30.
settings.chromastudio.recipeKey.tip: The key that looks up a block's recipe inside the window. Click, then press a key; Escape leaves it unbound.
settings.chromastudio.litematicaPlacemen: Where an exported schematic is placed: at the block you look at, or always where you stand.
give.chromastudio.no_world: This only works in a world.
give.chromastudio.no_permission: This needs creative mode or operator rights.
hotbar.chromastudio.nothing: None of these blocks has an item to hold.
hotbar.chromastudio.rest.slots: %s more went into free inventory slots.
hotbar.chromastudio.rest.box: %s more went into a shulker box.
hotbar.chromastudio.dropped: Blocks with no slot, dropped at your feet: %s.
hotbar.chromastudio.dropped_boxes: Shulker boxes with no slot, dropped at your feet: %s.
hotbar.chromastudio.left_out: Blocks left out, as the game drops only so many at once: %s.
hotbar.chromastudio.nothing_to_undo: There's no hotbar fill to undo.
hotbar.chromastudio.undone: Put your hotbar back as it was.
hotbar.chromastudio.undone_dropped: Put your inventory back as it was. What was dropped is still on the ground.
hotbar.chromastudio.no_permission: This needs creative mode or operator rights.
capture.chromastudio.keys: Press %s on a block. Escape cancels.
capture.chromastudio.too_big: That box is too big. The most a capture counts is %s blocks.
capture.chromastudio.empty: There's nothing but air in that box, in the chunks that are loaded.
capture.chromastudio.name: Capture %s %s %s to %s %s %s
capture.chromastudio.done: Captured a palette of %s blocks, from %s kinds found.
command.chromastudio.capture.usage: Give two corners: /chroma capture x1 y1 z1 x2 y2 z2
palettes.chromastudio.new.title: New palette
palettes.chromastudio.rename.title: Rename palette
palettes.chromastudio.delete.tip: Deletes this palette and its file.
palettes.chromastudio.delete.title: Delete palette
palettes.chromastudio.delete.question: Delete "%s"? Its file is removed and this can't be undone.
palettes.chromastudio.import.tip: Makes a palette from a share string or a JSON file.
palettes.chromastudio.import.title: Import a palette
palettes.chromastudio.import.hint: Paste a share string, or type a JSON file's path
palettes.chromastudio.import.empty: Paste a share string or give a file first.
palettes.chromastudio.share.tip: Copies this palette as one line of text to send to someone. Tags and notes aren't carried.
palettes.chromastudio.shared: Copied the share string. Tags and notes aren't in it.
palettes.chromastudio.copy.tip: Makes a copy of this palette that you can change.
palettes.chromastudio.no_dialog: No file dialog came up. Type the file's path instead.
palettes.chromastudio.no_world: This only works in a world.
palettes.chromastudio.need_entries: This palette has no blocks yet.
palettes.chromastudio.preset_fixed: Presets can't be changed. Copy this one to make it yours.
palettes.chromastudio.index_building: The block index is still being built. Try again in a moment.
palettes.chromastudio.search.tip: Lists only the palettes and presets whose name or tags have every word typed here.
palettes.chromastudio.none_selected: Pick a palette on the left, or make one with New, Generate, Capture or Image.
palettes.chromastudio.empty: No blocks yet. Add them with the + button on a Match result, or fill the palette with Generate, Capture or Image.
palettes.chromastudio.save_failed: The palette couldn't be saved. The log says why.
palettes.chromastudio.no_matches: No blocks matched under the default filters in the settings.
palettes.chromastudio.tags.tip: Words to find this palette by, separated by commas.
palettes.chromastudio.notes.tip: Anything you want to remember about this palette.
palettes.chromastudio.entry.weight.tip: How often this block turns up next to the others, in a diorama, an export or a WorldEdit pattern.
palettes.chromastudio.entry.unknown: %s isn't a block in this game. It's kept, and left out of exports.
palettes.chromastudio.tool.generate.tip: Makes a palette from a colour and a harmony.
palettes.chromastudio.tool.capture.tip: Makes a palette from the blocks in a box of the world. Pick two corners with the eyedropper key; click again to cancel.
palettes.chromastudio.tool.image.tip: Makes a palette from an image's main colours.
palettes.chromastudio.tool.analyse.tip: Looks for what this palette is missing, such as darks, highlights or an accent.
palettes.chromastudio.tool.diorama.tip: Shows this palette as a wall of blocks, flat or in 3D.
palettes.chromastudio.tool.export.tip: Writes this palette as a schematic.
palettes.chromastudio.tool.worldedit.tip: Builds a WorldEdit command from this palette.
palettes.chromastudio.tool.hotbar.tip: Puts this palette's blocks in your hotbar.
palettes.chromastudio.generate.title: Generate a palette
palettes.chromastudio.generate.in_hand.n: Hold a block to use its colour.
palettes.chromastudio.generate.roll.tip: Picks a colour and a harmony at random.
palettes.chromastudio.generate.bad_hex: That isn't a colour. Use six hex digits, like #ff8800.
palettes.chromastudio.generate.name: %s %s
palettes.chromastudio.image.title: Palette from an image
palettes.chromastudio.image.hint: Path to a PNG, JPEG, GIF or BMP
palettes.chromastudio.image.unreadable: %s isn't an image that can be read.
palettes.chromastudio.analyse.heading: Findings: %s
palettes.chromastudio.analyse.none: Nothing to fix: this palette is balanced.
palettes.chromastudio.analyse.fix.tip: Opens Match on a colour that would mend this.
palettes.chromastudio.analyse.explore.ti: Highlights this palette's blocks on the Explore tab.
palettes.chromastudio.diorama.view.tip: Flat tiles the blocks' textures. 3D draws the blocks themselves.
palettes.chromastudio.diorama.reroll.tip: Lays the wall out again, at random.
palettes.chromastudio.diorama.export.tip: Exports this very wall as a schematic.
palettes.chromastudio.export.title: Export a schematic
palettes.chromastudio.export.gap.na: The diorama layouts fill every cell, so they have no gaps.
palettes.chromastudio.export.height.na: Only the wall and the diorama layouts have a height.
palettes.chromastudio.export.width.na: Only the diorama layouts have a width.
palettes.chromastudio.export.patch.na: Only the patch grid has a patch size.
palettes.chromastudio.export.place.tip: Writes the file and places it in Litematica, selected and ready to move.
palettes.chromastudio.export.place.no_li: Litematica isn't installed, so there's nothing to place the schematic with.
palettes.chromastudio.export.place.nbt: Litematica places .litematic files. Change the format to place it.
palettes.chromastudio.worldedit.title: WorldEdit command
palettes.chromastudio.worldedit.from.nee: Type the blocks to replace first.
palettes.chromastudio.worldedit.send.tip: Sends the command as chat, as if you'd typed it. It needs WorldEdit on the server and a selection.
palettes.chromastudio.hotbar.title: Fill the hotbar
palettes.chromastudio.hotbar.about: Puts these %s blocks in your hotbar, from the first slot. Undo puts back what was there.
palettes.chromastudio.hotbar.about.never: Puts the first nine blocks in your hotbar and the other %s in free inventory slots. Any with no slot are dropped at your feet. Undo puts back what was there.
palettes.chromastudio.hotbar.about.when_: Puts the first nine blocks in your hotbar and the other %s in free inventory slots, with a shulker box for any with no slot. Undo puts back what was there.
palettes.chromastudio.hotbar.about.alway: Puts the first nine blocks in your hotbar and the other %s in shulker boxes in your inventory. Undo puts back what was there.
gradient.chromastudio.stop.tip: Click to select, drag to reorder, right-click to remove
gradient.chromastudio.stop.two_needed: A gradient needs at least two stops.
gradient.chromastudio.stop.hex.tip: A colour to add as a stop.
gradient.chromastudio.stop.add.tip: Adds this colour as a stop after the selected one.
gradient.chromastudio.stop.in_hand.tip: Adds the block you hold as a stop.
gradient.chromastudio.stop.full: A gradient has at most %s stops.
gradient.chromastudio.steps.tip: How many blocks the gradient has, from 2 to 32.
gradient.chromastudio.easing.tip: How the colours are spaced between the stops.
gradient.chromastudio.arc.tip: Which way round the colour wheel the hue goes between two stops.
gradient.chromastudio.spread.tip: Prefers blocks whose textures are as busy as the ends of the gradient.
gradient.chromastudio.filters.tip: The Match tab's other filters, which a gradient keeps to as well: it only uses blocks that pass them. %s now.
gradient.chromastudio.too_few: Only %s blocks pass the filters, and the gradient needs %s. Loosen the filters or use fewer steps.
gradient.chromastudio.failed: The gradient couldn't be worked out. The log says why.
gradient.chromastudio.action.hotbar.tip: Puts the gradient's blocks in your hotbar, in order.
gradient.chromastudio.action.copy.tip: Copies the blocks' ids, one to a line.
gradient.chromastudio.action.export.tip: Writes the gradient as a schematic, a strip by default.
gradient.chromastudio.action.save.tip: Makes a palette of the gradient's blocks.
chromastudio.analysis.narrow_range: The blocks are all close in lightness, so the build may look flat. Add something lighter or darker.
chromastudio.analysis.lightness_gap: There's a jump in lightness with nothing in between. A block in the middle would bridge it.
chromastudio.analysis.no_darks: There's nothing dark. A dark block gives shadows and outlines.
chromastudio.analysis.no_highlights: There's nothing light. A light block gives highlights.
chromastudio.analysis.hues_stray: The hues don't sit on one colour harmony. A block of the missing hue would tie them together.
chromastudio.analysis.no_accent: Every block is muted. One saturated block would give the eye somewhere to land.
chromastudio.analysis.too_saturated: Most of the blocks are strongly coloured. Something muted would give them room.
chromastudio.analysis.accent_contrast: The most colourful block is as light as the rest, so it won't stand out. A lighter or darker accent would.
chromastudio.analysis.too_busy: Most of the textures are busy. A calmer, grainy block would rest the eye.
chromastudio.analysis.texture_jump: The textures jump from flat to busy. A grainy block would sit between them.
chromastudio.analysis.too_small: With fewer than three blocks there's little to vary.
chromastudio.analysis.too_large: With more than twelve blocks a build can lose its look. Consider splitting the palette.
match.chromastudio.hex.tip: The colour as a hex code, like #FF8800.
match.chromastudio.rgb.tip: Red, green and blue, each from 0 to 255.
match.chromastudio.hsl.tip: Hue from 0 to 360, then saturation and lightness from 0 to 100.
match.chromastudio.pick_block.tip: Closes the window so you can pick a block in the world. Look at one and press %s; the window comes back on it.
match.chromastudio.pick_screen.tip: Picks a colour from anywhere on screen. The window steps aside; click what you want, or press Escape to call it off.
match.chromastudio.dye.tip: Gives a dyeable item, such as leather armour, in exactly this colour.
match.chromastudio.slot.tip: Click to match the block you're holding.
match.chromastudio.slot.tip.scroll: Scroll to go through your hotbar.
match.chromastudio.face.tip: The face of each block to compare. Side is the best of the four sides; Any is the best of all six.
match.chromastudio.metric.tip: How the difference between two colours is measured. OKLab matches what the eye sees.
match.chromastudio.grid.tip: Shows the results as a grid of textures rather than a list.
match.chromastudio.distance.tip: How far away you'll look at the build. Further away, a texture's detail blurs together. Drag, or scroll to step.
match.chromastudio.distance.scale: At this distance a block face shows about %s texels across. The marks are where that halves.
match.chromastudio.biome.tip: Where grass, leaves and water get their tint: where you stand, a biome you choose, or where you stand with each block's range across every biome shown under its name.
match.chromastudio.biome.pick.tip: The chosen biome is %s. Click to choose another.
match.chromastudio.biome.pick.off: Set the biome control to Chosen to pick a biome.
match.chromastudio.find_biome.tip: Lists the five biomes that bring this block closest to the last colour you matched.
match.chromastudio.find_biome.no_block: Find biome needs a tinted block, such as grass or leaves, as the target. Pick one with the eyedropper or the item slot.
match.chromastudio.find_biome.no_colour: Match a colour first: Find biome looks for the biome that brings the block closest to it.
match.chromastudio.find_biome.use: Click to match in this biome.
match.chromastudio.filter.kind.tip: The kind of block to list, such as slabs or stairs.
match.chromastudio.filter.solid.tip: Only blocks you can't walk through.
match.chromastudio.filter.opaque.tip: Only blocks you can't see through.
match.chromastudio.filter.more.tip: More filters: mods, tone, lightness, chroma and texture. Lit while any of them is narrowing the results.
match.chromastudio.filter.same_texture.t: Only blocks that look the same from every side.
match.chromastudio.filter.tinted.tip: Blocks whose colour depends on the biome, such as grass and leaves.
Blocks you can't get in survival, such as bedrock.
match.chromastudio.filter.technical.tip: Blocks with no item in the creative inventory.
match.chromastudio.filter.block_entity.t: Blocks the game draws without a block model, such as chests, banners, shulker boxes and heads. Their colour is a guess from the texture they break into, so they are left out unless this is on.
match.chromastudio.filter.tone.tip: Only warm, cool or neutral colours.
match.chromastudio.filter.lightness.tip: The darkest and lightest to list, from 0 to 1.
match.chromastudio.filter.chroma.tip: The dullest and most vivid to list, from 0 to 0.4. At 0.4 there's no upper limit.
match.chromastudio.filter.badge.tip: Only textures that are this flat or busy. With none lit, all are listed.
match.chromastudio.filter.reset.tip: Puts every filter back to how the settings start them.
match.chromastudio.filter.mods.tip: List only this mod's blocks, or leave them out.
match.chromastudio.row.tinted: Tinted by the game, as grass is by its biome.
match.chromastudio.row.gradient: Right-click to start a gradient from it.
match.chromastudio.row.add: Ctrl-click to add it to the current palette.
match.chromastudio.row.swap: Click for the next-best blocks to swap in.
match.chromastudio.swap.none: Nothing else of this kind passes the filters.
match.chromastudio.set.tip: Show the other blocks of this material.
match.chromastudio.make_palette: Make a palette of these %s blocks
match.chromastudio.make_palette.tip: Makes a new palette from this material's blocks and selects it.
match.chromastudio.recipe.none: Install JEI, REI or EMI to look up recipes.
explore.chromastudio.chroma.min.tip: The dullest blocks to plot, from 0 to 0.4. It's the Match tab's chroma filter.
explore.chromastudio.chroma.max.tip: The most vivid blocks to plot. At 0.4 there's no upper limit.
explore.chromastudio.reset_view.tip: Zooms back out to every hue and lightness.
explore.chromastudio.clear_highlight.tip: Stops ringing the blocks of the analysed palette.
explore.chromastudio.clear_highlight.non: No palette is highlighted. Analyse one in the Palettes tab to ring its blocks here.
eyedropper.chromastudio.no_block.how: Look at a block and press the key again.
eyedropper.chromastudio.not_ready: The block index is still being built
eyedropper.chromastudio.not_indexed.how: Blocks with no texture of their own, such as air, have no colour to read.
picker.chromastudio.hint: Click to pick the colour under the cursor. Escape cancels.
give.chromastudio.disabled: %s is switched off in this world.
